package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling theft of sensitive credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of credential harvesting and exfiltration logic.

attack_chain.action: The code reads sensitive files from the user's home directory, specifically ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of private SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are sent via HTTPS POST to the attacker's server at app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to an external attacker-controlled domain.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config.
The package sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com containing file contents.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config and posts data to an external domain
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to /upload endpoint on app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that trigger file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config during setup.py execution, combined with outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com. Flag any package whose setup.py contains code that reads these files and transmits their contents to external domains.
